evaluation.positioning_hook: A teleporting father races through a downtown office tower to rescue his imprisoned six-year-old daughter before a ruthless black-site team collars her powers.

audience_appeal_marketability.reasoning: The emotional promise is immediate: a father trying to save his little girl under extreme pressure. The teleportation mechanic, the ticking rescue, and the child-in-danger setup give it clean genre appeal with a strong trailer-ready spine.

conceptual_hook_clarity.reasoning: The premise lands fast and stays legible: James can teleport, Rosie can eventually do the same, and a covert team is trying to contain them. The black app, the clapping code, and the blind jump concept make the engine easy to track.

character_appeal_and_long_term_potential.reasoning: James is built as a desperate, protective father with a dangerous edge, and Rosie gives the story its emotional center. Nora, Davidson, and Edgar add pressure and texture, with the father-daughter bond doing most of the heavy lifting.

creative_originality_and_boldness.reasoning: The script takes a familiar rescue-thriller frame and gives it a clean sci-fi rule set with a child’s-eye emotional logic. The clapping communication, blind-jump physics, and rooftop-to-sky escalation give it a confident, playable identity.

narrative_momentum_engagement.reasoning: It moves with real urgency, constantly shifting location, pressure, and tactical advantage. Each beat escalates the rescue, and the final airborne sequence turns the premise into a sustained survival set piece.

resonant_originality.reasoning: A teleporting parent trying to coach a terrified child through a power escape has a fresh, emotionally intuitive core. It feels immediately understandable while still carrying enough invention to stand apart in the genre lane.

world_density_and_texture.reasoning: The world is specific in its covert-tech details, office-building geography, and black-site surveillance culture. It’s more of a pressure-cooker container than a sprawling universe, but the rules are clear and story-generating.

tonal_specificity.reasoning: The tone blends thriller urgency with a deeply vulnerable parent-child dynamic, then spikes into violent sci-fi action. The contrast between childlike fear and tactical brutality gives the piece a distinct emotional temperature.

latent_depth_slow_burn_potential.reasoning: Beneath the rescue mechanics, there are hints of a larger history: the mother’s death, the family’s persecution, and the ethics of power containment. The script suggests a bigger mythology without needing to over-explain it.

relationship_density_and_ensemble_engine.reasoning: The engine is strongest in the James-Rosie bond, with Nora, Davidson, and Edgar functioning as a compact pressure system around them. The relationships are effective and playable, though the story is fundamentally driven by one central dyad.

casting_characteristics: Female child lead around 6 years old
Older male authority figure in his 60s
Physically capable supporting male in his 30s
Physically capable supporting male in his 30s-40s

notable_requirements: Downtown Los Angeles office tower interiors

technical.vfx_details: Teleportation effects, electric bursts, sky/fall continuity, and a few materialization beats require compositing and cleanup.
technical.sfx_needs: Collar effects, stun-gun hits, rubber bullet impacts, practical blood hit, and controlled falls/physical struggle.

platform_fit.recommended_lane: streaming thriller lane or contained theatrical genre lane
platform_fit.series_engine_or_release_model: Feature release model: contained, high-concept genre piece with strong trailer moments and a clear emotional hook.

cost.note: Contemporary locations keep it contained, but teleportation VFX, rooftop work, and the airborne finale push it above micro-budget.

cast.note: The project depends on a strong child performance and a compact adult ensemble with clear authority and physicality.

location.note: Mostly contained to a few interiors and rooftops, with one major sky/fall sequence that adds logistical complexity.

content.note: The material includes child endangerment, violent confrontations, and a death-by-materialization beat that narrows the family lane.

rights.note: No named music, brands, or real-person references drive the story.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The father-daughter bond is the engine.
strengths.what_it_means: This is not just a chase premise; it’s a rescue story powered by parental desperation and a child’s trust. That gives the material emotional immediacy and a clear audience promise beyond the sci-fi mechanics.
strengths.evidence: James coaching Rosie through claps, jumps, and the final airborne rescue.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The teleportation rule set is clean and playable.
strengths.what_it_means: The script gives the audience a simple, visual power system with understandable limits: line-of-sight, memory, ceramic interference, and physical consequence. That clarity makes the action easy to follow and easy to market.
strengths.evidence: The black app map, the line-of-sight explanation, and the collar blocking powers.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The child perspective makes the sci-fi feel human.
strengths.what_it_means: Rosie’s fear, literal thinking, and need for reassurance turn the genre concept into something emotionally legible. It creates a rare blend of spectacle and vulnerability that actors and audiences can both latch onto.
strengths.evidence: Rosie clapping yes/no, begging for Mommy, and resisting the blind jump.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The contained setting keeps the tension tight.
strengths.what_it_means: An office tower, a holding cell, a monitor room, and a rooftop give the story a producible footprint while still feeling cinematic. It’s a pressure-cooker design that supports momentum without requiring a sprawling world.
strengths.evidence: The action stays centered in one building complex and adjacent rooftops.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The antagonists have a crisp institutional vibe.
strengths.what_it_means: Nora, Davidson, and Edgar feel like a believable covert apparatus rather than generic villains. That gives the story a professional, tactical texture that elevates the threat and helps the world feel lived-in.
strengths.evidence: The monitor room, tactical teams, collar protocol, and Davidson’s command style.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The finale delivers a strong visual payoff.
strengths.what_it_means: The sky-fall sequence is a built-in trailer moment: a child plummeting, repeated jumps, and a physics-defying rescue. It gives the script a memorable climax that can sell the premise in a single image.
strengths.evidence: Rosie’s repeated midair blips and James catching her above the city.

whats_special.headline: BLIND JUMP is a tight, emotionally charged sci-fi rescue thriller built around a father and six-year-old daughter with a terrifying shared power. It has a clean concept, a producible footprint, and a finale that turns the premise into a genuinely cinematic set piece.

lead_characters.name: JAMES
lead_characters.hook: James is an everyman with a dangerous gift and a father’s panic running underneath every move. He’s tactical, exhausted, and emotionally exposed all at once — the kind of man who can coach a child through a life-or-death escape while carrying the guilt of a family catastrophe he can’t undo. He reads as someone who has lived inside fear long enough to make it look like competence.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is a showcase for controlled intensity, paternal tenderness, and physical urgency in one role. An actor gets to play the emotional center of a high-concept thriller while also carrying action beats and moral heat, in the same broad lane as the grounded desperation of Casey Affleck in Manchester by the Sea or the protective volatility of Joel Edgerton in The Gift.

lead_characters.name: ROSIE
lead_characters.hook: Rosie is a little girl forced to process terror with the tools of a child: literal thinking, obedience, fear, and flashes of courage. She’s not a plot device; she’s the emotional pulse of the piece, and her innocence makes the world around her feel more dangerous. Her arc is about trust becoming bravery in real time.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: For a young performer, this is a rare part that asks for fear, confusion, trust, and release without ever losing the audience. It has the same kind of heartbreaking immediacy that makes child performances in Room or The Florida Project linger, while still giving the actor a clear emotional journey.

lead_characters.name: NORA
lead_characters.hook: Nora is the cold professional in the room, all training, surveillance discipline, and controlled menace. She’s smart enough to anticipate James, but she’s also human enough to register the moral pressure of what she’s doing, which gives her a sharp, watchable edge. She feels like someone who has spent years turning empathy into procedure.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is a strong antagonist/supporting role for an actor who likes precision and authority with a crack of humanity underneath. It offers the kind of contained, high-tension performance space that can land like Rebecca Ferguson in Mission: Impossible or Carrie Coon in a more severe register.

lead_characters.name: DAVIDSON
lead_characters.hook: Davidson is the polished institutional predator: calm, managerial, and lethal by delegation. He doesn’t need to raise his voice to dominate a room, and that makes him especially dangerous. He’s the face of a system that can talk about civility while preparing a child for autopsy.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is a delicious authority role for an actor who can weaponize restraint. It sits in the same performance space as the quiet menace of Bryan Cranston in Trumbo or the corporate chill of Michael Stuhlbarg in a more controlled register.

lead_characters.name: EDGAR
lead_characters.hook: Edgar is the physical wildcard inside the machine — intense, athletic, and emotionally compromised because the child is his blood. He gives the story a volatile human fracture inside the tactical apparatus, and when he turns, it matters. He’s the one character whose body can break the system open.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is a strong supporting role for an actor with physical presence who wants a pressure-cooker turn with a moral pivot. It has the kinetic charge of a late-breaking ally in a thriller, with the emotional charge of a family member trying to outrun the institution.

director_appeal.hook: A director who wants to stage intimate emotion inside a clean, high-concept action engine.
director_appeal.detail: The material rewards precision: spatial clarity, escalating pressure, and a finale that has to feel both physically legible and emotionally earned. It’s especially attractive to a filmmaker who can make contained locations feel expansive and can balance spectacle with genuine parental panic.

buyer_appeal.lane: contained streaming thriller / genre-forward indie lane
buyer_appeal.detail: This fits a buyer looking for a high-concept, emotionally accessible genre piece that can be made without a giant footprint. The cast is compact, the locations are manageable, and the premise is easy to communicate in one sentence, which is exactly what helps a contained thriller travel.

considerations.area: The concept plays cleanly in a feature runtime.
considerations.detail: The premise is strong enough to carry a full-length thriller, and the final airborne sequence gives it a clear feature-scale climax. Packaging should lean into the contained footprint and the father-daughter emotional hook.

considerations.area: The child lead is the emotional and casting center.
considerations.detail: Rosie is the role that will determine the movie’s heartbeat, so the casting search should prioritize a young performer who can hold fear, trust, and literal comedy in the same frame. Protecting that performance will protect the whole piece.

considerations.area: The office-tower geography is a major asset.
considerations.detail: The building layout, rooftop access, and monitor-room pressure create a contained action map that is easy to stage and easy for an audience to follow. One direction would be to keep that spatial logic foregrounded in any future pass, because it’s doing a lot of narrative work.

considerations.area: The final sky sequence is the signature set piece.
considerations.detail: The repeated jumps and midair rescue are the most cinematic stretch of the script, and they justify the feature frame. In production terms, that sequence should be protected as the visual centerpiece, since it’s the moment that turns the premise into an event.

considerations.area: The tone sits between thriller and family drama.
considerations.detail: That blend is one of the script’s most attractive qualities, and it will help the movie reach beyond pure genre buyers. A future pass could continue to foreground the emotional stakes as much as the tactical ones, because that balance is what makes the concept feel special.
